title: kv: span compaction guided evictor and workload-feedback eviction heuristic
author: Asha Patel
body:
Motivation: Large, long-lived KV cache backends at heavy traffic reveal two correlated problems: (1) fragmentation of cached spans that prevents efficient reclamation of contiguous memory leading to frequent small spills to disk, and (2) static eviction scoring that does not adapt to shifting workload patterns (prefix-heavy vs tail-heavy access). This PR introduces a span-compaction-aware evictor and an online workload-feedback loop that biases eviction scoring to reduce fragmentation, reduce spillover churn, and improve tail latency under mixed workloads.

Design summary: single-threaded changes in eviction hot path are intentionally small; core behavior changes are: (A) SpanCompactor: a background compaction pass that opportunistically coalesces adjacent free spans when fragmentation crosses a tunable threshold, avoiding expensive full defrag during critical windows. Compaction is bounded by a budget (max_bytes per second and max_spans per cycle) and coordinated with the scheduler to avoid impacting per-request latency SLOs. (B) WorkloadFeedbackEvictor: eviction scoring extended with a short-term access histogram (micro-window) and a drift-corrected recency-weight, so frequently reaccessed small spans receive a temporary retention boost while cold large spans are prioritized for coalescing and eviction. (C) EarlySpillBackoff: when disk spill rates spike, policy throttles low-value evictions and increases compaction budget for short periods to reduce repeated spill-churn. (D) Telemetry: new metrics (kv.compaction.runs, kv.compaction.bytes_moved, kv.eviction.score_histogram, kv.spill.retries) and a diagnostic route to snapshot current span map for debugging.

Compatibility notes: all on-disk cache formats unchanged. Configuration knobs are behind a runtime flag feature.kv_span_compactor=false by default; rollouts can enable per-cluster. The compactor is safe on dedicated and private deployments; code paths include guardrails for air-gapped environments (no external calls).

Benchmarks: microbench harness runs with mix of synthetic workloads (50% small hot keys, 50% long-tail scans) measured on our perf lab NVMe+A100 nodes showed: median latency unchanged, p95 tail latency reduced 12% under mixed load, overall spillover events reduced 22%, and peak memory overhead improved by ~18% due to reduced fragmentation. End-to-end token-cost for a continuous-batching scenario with heavy KV cache reuse dropped ~6% after tuning. These numbers are reproducible with the included benchmark script in perf-canary/.

What changed (high level file areas): additions in runtime/kv/cache_compactor.{cc,h}, runtime/kv/evictor_feedback.{cc,h}, runtime/kv/metrics_registry.cc, runtime/scheduler/priority_hints.cc, config/defaults.yaml (new knobs), tests/kv/compactor_integration_test.cc, perf-canary/kv_fragmentation_bench.py, docs/observability/kv_compaction.md. Small public API additions: new config keys under kv.compaction.{enabled,bytes_per_sec,max_spans_cycle} and kv.eviction.feedback_window_ms.

Commit summary: - initial span compactor scaffolding and basic compaction loop - implement coalescing heuristics and budget framework - add workload-feedback histogram and merge into eviction scoring - integrate with scheduler via priority hints to pause compaction during high tail request load - metrics, tests, and perf harness - documentation and rollout guide - two follow-up fixes for race in compaction shutdown and test flakiness.

Files changed (high level): runtime/kv/cache_compactor.cc: new compaction loop and coalescer logic; runtime/kv/cache_compactor.h: interfaces and budget struct; runtime/kv/evictor_feedback.cc/.h: histogram and scoring integration; runtime/kv/kv_store.cc: hooks into eviction path and early-spill backoff; runtime/scheduler/priority_hints.cc: new pause/resume for background tasks; tests/kv/*: integration tests and race reproducer; perf-canary/*: reproducible benchmark scripts and configs; docs/observability/kv_compaction.md: telemetry and runbook.

Review conversation (high level): - Diego: requested clarifications on compaction budget interplay with autoscaler. Asha: added a scheduler hook so compaction budgets are halved when autoscaler signals high load; included unit tests. - Lina: flagged potential race on shutdown where compactor could touch freed spans; Asha: added a graceful checkpoint and a mutex/epoch guard and two tests that reproduce and verify fix. - Marcus: asked for more metrics around spill retries and a view into span histogram; Asha: added kv.spill.retries and an admin endpoint to snapshot span map. - Diego: ran perf lab numbers and asked for reproducibility artifacts; Asha: uploaded perf scripts and dockerfile for harness in perf-canary. Final approvals after minor test naming nits.

CI status: initial run failed on macOS lint (line-length in docs) and on a flaky integration test (compactor_shutdown_test). Fixes: docs lint fixed, added retry/timeout in test; subsequent CI run: all checks passed (build, unit, integration, perf-smoke).

Merging: squash-and-merge with a single commit message summarizing span compactor + feedback evictor; changelog entry added to release notes. Rollout plan: enable feature.kv_span_compactor in canary for 48h, monitor kv.compaction.* and kv.spill.* metrics for regressions, then widen to 10% then 50%.

Follow-ups (open todos): - autotune heuristics for feedback_window_ms per workload class (ENG-1987) - add a bounded multi-threaded compactor option for very large caches (future perf investigation) - integrate compaction budget signals with Dedicated autoscaler more tightly.

If you want to reproduce: see perf-canary/README.md for setup and perf-canary/kv_fragmentation_bench.py for the workloads used to generate bench numbers.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: This looks promising. Can you describe how compaction interacts with the autoscaler? We need to make sure compaction doesn't push the system into extra nodes in the middle of canary.
Asha Patel: Added scheduler hook to halve compaction budget on autoscaler high-load signals. See runtime/scheduler/priority_hints.cc and tests for behavior.
Lina Zhou: Found a race on shutdown where compactor touched freed spans in the store. Can we add an epoch or graceful drain?
Asha Patel: Added epoch guard and compactor checkpointing, plus an integration test that reproduces the previous flake.
Marcus Reed: Please expose spill retry metric and a snapshot endpoint for span map; helps debugging customer incidents.
Asha Patel: Added kv.spill.retries and admin span snapshot route under debug/admin/kv_span_map.
release_notes: Introduce span compactor and workload-feedback evictor: reduces KV fragmentation and spillover, improves p95 under mixed workloads. Feature gated behind kv.compaction.enabled; rollout plan in docs/observability/kv_compaction.md.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature.kv_span_compactor=false by default. When enabling, follow rollout plan: canary 48h -> 10% -> 50%. Monitor kv.compaction.runs, kv.compaction.bytes_moved, kv.spill.retries, and kv.eviction.score_histogram. If spill.retries increase >20% from baseline, rollback and increase compaction budget.
